I'm planning a JUnit 4 test class for UnsupportedDurationField aiming for maximum branch coverage, starting by analyzing the getInstance(type) method's caching logic—checking null cache initialization, field lookup on cache hit, and behavior with different type values across repeated calls.

I'm also mapping out other methods needing coverage: compareTo's isSupported branching, equals' multiple conditions (identity check, instanceof check, and a null name check that's likely unreachable given DurationFieldType's actual implementation), plus simple getters and the UnsupportedOperationException-throwing methods that need individual verification. I'm noting that since junit 3.8 is on the classpath rather than 4.11+, I can't rely on @FixMethodOrder to control test execution order for covering the static cCache's null-vs-populated branches.

Since cCache is static and shared, I'm realizing I can't cleanly reset it between tests, so verifying the "first call populates cache" branch is tricky without using a fresh, previously-untouched DurationFieldType for each relevant test.

Instead, I could use different DurationFieldType values across tests to avoid interference, and verify caching behavior by calling getInstance twice with the same type and checking for identical instances returned. For the specific branch where cCache is null, I plan to use reflection to forcibly reset that static field to null before the test, then call getInstance and confirm it rebuilds the cache correctly.

I'll also design tests to check the field==null (cache miss) path by resetting the cache and requesting a fresh type, then the cache hit path by calling again with the same type and asserting reference equality. A third test will confirm two distinct types produce two distinct cached instances.

Beyond caching, I need tests for getType, getName matching the type's name, isSupported returning false, isPrecise returning true, and getUnitMillis returning zero. I also need to verify that all the value/difference/add/millis conversion methods correctly throw UnsupportedOperationException since this field doesn't support those operations.

For compareTo tests, I'm thinking through how to get a real supported DurationField instance without Mockito available -- maybe using ISOChronology's millis field or a standard DurationFieldType getter instead of mocking.

For equals tests, same-instance, different-type-object, and equal-names cases: checking whether the private constructor and caching behavior in getInstance means two separate creations of the same type will actually return identical cached objects, which matters for the equals comparison tests.

The reflection approach also handles the false case with mismatched type names. As for the branch where other.getName() is null, I realize that's unreachable since DurationFieldType is abstract with factory methods always returning non-null names, so I'll leave that branch untested with a note explaining why. Then I still need hashCode, toString, and serialization readResolve tests confirming singleton behavior survives round-tripping.

I'm also considering what happens with getInstance(null) - the cache would store a null key fine, but calling getName() later would NPE since the type itself is null. That's worth a dedicated test to confirm the null-key caching behavior.

With that settled, I'm ready to write the full test class, including the needed imports for reflection, DurationField, ISOChronology, and serialization utilities.

Since JUnit doesn't guarantee test order, resetting the cache fully might wipe entries other tests rely on, but as long as each test only checks identity within itself, that's safe to ignore. For the cache-hit scenario I don't need a reset—just invoke the method twice in the same test; for the "different types yield different instances" test, no reset is needed either, just plain calls.

I'll pick two distinct DurationFieldType factory methods not reused elsewhere (like halfdays and centuries) to avoid collisions, then verify they produce different objects while each equals itself.
